summary: Short onboarding call focused on NovaMed's SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture and getting the NovaMed compliance team read-only access to Redwood's Trust Portal. We reviewed high level controls, RBAC/SSO approach, audit logging and retention, KMS/encryption patterns, and data residency constraints. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-28
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (NovaMed CISO), Elliot Huang (NovaMed Head IT), Sofia Torres (NovaMed Compliance), Amir Khan (NovaMed Cloud)

Auto-summary (auto): quick onboarding, portal access, plan control mapping, send reports

00:00 - Lena Park: Hey everybody, thanks for joining — this is Lena from Redwood, and with me is Marco, our SE. How's everyone doing?
00:36 - Priya Raman: Hi all, thanks. Busy day but ready. We wanted to make sure we get an understanding of what evidence and access you provide before the audit kickoff.
01:12 - Marco Silva: Great, Priya. We'll cover the Trust Portal access, what artifacts are available — SOC 2 Type II, ISO cert — and the RBAC model for read-only viewers vs admin roles. Quick note: sometimes our transcript system shows "trust center" and "trust portal" interchangeably, sorry if there's confusion.
02:10 - Elliot Huang: One ask up front — we have strict data residency reqs for EU patient data. We'll need to confirm where logs and snapshots live.
03:05 - Marco Silva: Yep, understood. Redwood Hosted keeps region metadata per request; for Dedicated or Private you can pin region or run on-prem. For hosted, we can restrict model serving to eu-central-1 for example, and audit logs include region tags.
04:00 - Priya Raman: Can you point me to the actual SOC 2 report? Who attests?
04:22 - Lena Park: Sure — we'll share the signed Type II report today. It's in the Trust Portal. Link: https://app.redwood.example/trust-portal (we'll send a read-only grant).
05:50 - Marco Silva: About RBAC, our default roles are: viewer (read-only), operator (deploy/scale), admin. Viewer gets access to logs and reports but can't change deployment configs. We also map IdP groups via SAML so you can keep group-based access.
06:40 - Sofia Torres: For the audit we'll need evidence owners mapped to controls, ideally an owner per A.2 and A.9 type control — is that something Redwood can help map?
07:12 - Marco Silva: Yes, we usually run a control-mapping workshop where we go control-by-control and map Redwood artifacts (configuration, logs, runbooks) to ISO / SOC controls. We'll coordinate next week.
08:30 - Amir Khan: Quick technical Q: what's your KMS model? Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)?
09:10 - Marco Silva: We support both; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via our KMS integration (we support AWS KMS + HSM-backed keys in dedicated/private). In practice we rotate roots automatically and you can bring keys. There might be a small integration step to expose a KMS endpoint.
10:05 - Priya Raman: Ok, do you store any plaintext data for logs or traces that would be covered under PHI?
10:40 - Marco Silva: We don't retain user payloads beyond configured retention windows. The default for logs is 90 days; we can extend or export to your SIEM. Sensitive payloads can be redacted before storage — there are knobs for that.
12:05 - Lena Park: Real quick, who on NovaMed will own procurement? Is there a timeline for a PO/contract?
12:30 - Priya Raman: Procurement is looped in but looks like late Q4 is realistic for contract sign — maybe mid-November. We want the audit evidence before then but we can run the mapping and tech work in parallel.
14:00 - Elliot Huang: Regarding logs, what's the export format to our SIEM? Can we get a streaming export?
14:28 - Marco Silva: Yes, we support streaming via syslog/HTTP to your SIEM, and S3-compatible export of raw logs in NDJSON. There's also a connector for common SIEMs; we'll share config snippets.
15:35 - Priya Raman: About the Trust Portal access — we want read-only for compliance folks and a separate operator role for our infra team.
16:00 - Lena Park: That matches our role model. Marco will set those permissions and we can show a quick screen-share of Trust Portal role assignment if helpful.
17:10 - Marco Silva: Small gotcha: the portal's RBAC names are case-sensitive and when mapping SAML groups we recommend naming convention like nm-compliance, nm-ops.
18:30 - Sofia Torres: For the control evidence, do you have pre-bundled artifacts for SOC 2 common criteria? Like configuration snapshots or runbooks?
19:02 - Marco Silva: Yep — the portal includes a controls bundle: config exports, patch history, access logs, incident playbooks, and SOC 2 attestation pack. For ISO we include info security policy and scope docs. These are the ones we typically map to controls.
20:45 - Amir Khan: How do you handle key rotation and access logs for keys?
21:10 - Marco Silva: Key rotation can be customer-driven or automatic; we can emit KMS audit logs to your logging endpoint and include the key rotation events in the Trust Portal audit stream.
22:55 - Priya Raman: Is there an SLA for evidence retrieval during an audit? We need timely access to logs and the attestation docs.
23:30 - Lena Park: For Dedicated and Private customers we have SLA-backed access windows. For Hosted, the Trust Portal is available 24/7 for read-only. We'll commit to turnaround times for ad-hoc requests in the SOW.
25:10 - Elliot Huang: Any compliance certifications or privacy addendums we should expect? DPAs?
25:40 - Marco Silva: We provide a DPA, data processing addendum, and can include subprocessors list. We'll also provide details for data residency, contractual PII handling.
26:55 - Sofia Torres: On retention — we may need 7 years of certain logs for regulatory reasons. Can you archive logs that long?
27:30 - Marco Silva: Yes, we can archive to long term cold storage exports; cost model differs. We'll include estimate in the pricing follow-up.
28:40 - Priya Raman: Can we get a short demo of the Trust Portal now? Even just the read-only report view.
29:05 - Lena Park: Sure, Marco can share screen — do you want to walk through the SOC 2 pack?
30:15 - Marco Silva: Sharing screen... (screen share noise) Ok so on the left nav there's Compliance -> Reports. Here's the SOC 2 Type II PDF, the ISO certificate, and the controls bundle. The evidence attachments show timestamps and related runbook links.
31:45 - Priya Raman: The timestamps are helpful; can we filter by region for logs?
32:15 - Marco Silva: Yes, upper-right filter allows region and model instance ID; for Hosted we tag by region, for Dedicated you'll see the dedicated cluster name.
33:50 - Amir Khan: About SSO — do you support IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows? Our Okta setup prefers IdP-initiated.
34:20 - Marco Silva: We support both; SAML mapping is flexible. We also have SCIM for provisioning users if you want to automate adds/removes.
35:50 - Elliot Huang: Any known gaps in YOUR SOC 2 that we should note? I mean, is there anything in the report that calls out partial controls?
36:20 - Lena Park: There was a minor control remediation last quarter around change management timing; the Type II report notes the closure. We'll flag that in the docs we send.
37:40 - Sofia Torres: For the mapping workshop, can you provide an initial pre-mapped spreadsheet to speed the session?
38:05 - Marco Silva: Absolutely — we'll send a pre-populated spreadsheet mapping common controls to Redwood artifacts so you can fill owners before the session.
39:30 - Priya Raman: On KMS details, we'd like example terraform or ARM snippets for integrating our KMS.
40:05 - Marco Silva: I'll attach Terraform snippets in the KMS guide and include sample IAM policies.
41:20 - Lena Park: Time check — we've got about 6 minutes left. Recap key blockers: procurement timeline and KMS integration spike. Everything else seems operational.
42:00 - Priya Raman: Correct. Also confirm that logs will be redact-able and we can set retention per log class.
42:25 - Marco Silva: Yes, retention policies per log type; redaction hooks can run before storage. We'll document the API for that.
43:10 - Amir Khan: We'll run a short test with KMS in a sandbox after we get the Terraform.
43:40 - Marco Silva: Perfect. I'll provision a sandbox keyflow diagram and sample endpoint.
44:20 - Lena Park: Ok final quick ask — can we aim to have the Trust Portal access done by Friday?
44:35 - Marco Silva: I can do that; I'll add Priya and Sofia as read-only and confirm via email.
45:00 - Priya Raman: Great, thanks.
45:30 - Sofia Torres: Appreciate it, this is helpful.
46:10 - Lena Park: Thanks everyone. We'll send the SOC2/ISO artifacts and the pre-mapped control spreadsheet, plus the KMS snippets. Expect an email from Marco with links and formal next steps.
47:10 - Marco Silva: Noted. I'll follow up with the portal invite and the Terraform examples.
47:40 - Lena Park: Meeting adjourned — thanks all.

Post-call notes (auto): Next: send artifacts, grant portal access, schedule mapping workshop.
